metadata.title: Channel Theory for Polynomial Continued Fractions: Asymptotic Channels, the ξ₀ = 2/√β₂ Identity, and a Bridge Conjecture
metadata.description:
Version notice (v1.7). This version corrects and attributes; it alters no theorem, proposition or numerical value of v1.6. Concept DOI is preserved (10.5281/zenodo.19941678); v1.6 (10.5281/zenodo.22782807) is superseded. It is a description-only version; the paragraph immediately below states what that means for the attached file.

The file attached to v1.7 is the v1.6 build, unchanged. The v1.7 corrections are recorded in this description only. v1.7 is a description-only new version: no PDF was rebuilt, and none is claimed to have been. The v1.4–v1.6 LaTeX sources are not in the working repository, and the only source held is v1.3.1 — a build made from it would silently revert two versions of corrections, including the Painlevé-target correction made at v1.4 and the analytic residual added at v1.6, both of which this notice relies on. Attaching a build that cannot be verified is the v1.6 defect (1) repeated; not attaching one is the avoidable choice, and it is the one taken. If the v1.6 sources or PDF become available and an updated build is wanted, that is v1.8.

0. Current state

This section is the whole current state. Nothing below it is needed to know what Channel Theory now asserts; §1 is history and §2–§7 are the detail.

Proven. For Q_n = b(n)Q_{n−1} + Q_{n−2} with Q_{−1} = 0, Q_0 = 1, deg b = d ≥ 1 and b(k) ≠ 0 for k ≥ 1:

— the normalised ratio r_n = Q_n/∏_{k≤n} b(k) converges unconditionally, with r_∞ − r_n = O(n^{−(2d−1)});

— if b(n) > 0 for all n ≥ 1 then 1 ≤ r_∞ ≤ exp Σ_{k≥1} 1/(b(k)b(k+1)) < ∞, so the hypothesis (H): r_∞ ≠ 0 holds automatically and is two-sidedly bounded;

— under (H), lim |Q_n/(dn)!|^{1/n} = |β_d|/d^d, hence B(w) = Σ_n Q_n w^n/Γ(dn+1) has radius d^d/|β_d| and, in the uniformiser ζ = w^{1/d}, ξ₀ = d/|β_d|^{1/d};

— Q_n/Γ(dn+1) = K (β_d/d^d)^n n^s (1 + O(1/n)) with s = β_{d−1}/β_d + (d−1)/2.

Attributed, not claimed. The radius identity — i.e. the statement carried since v1.0 as prop:xi0 at d = 2 and promoted at v1.3 to Conjecture 3.3.A★ — is a corollary of the Perron–Kreuser theorem together with Pincherle's minimal/dominant dichotomy. The conjecture label is retired: the statement is not a conjecture, it is classical, and the cross-degree formula ξ₀ = d/|β_d|^{1/d} now holds at every d ≥ 1 as a proved statement rather than at d = 2 proven / d = 4 verified (§2).

Verified, never proven. The closed form K = r_∞ (2π)^{(d−1)/2} / (√d · ∏_i Γ(1 − r_i)), where b(n) = β_d ∏_i (n − r_i) (§4). It agrees with computation to 109–115 decimal digits over eight test polynomials spanning d = 2, 3, 4, with a vacuity control that collapses the agreement to ≤ 0.75 digits when the ∏_i Γ(1 − r_i) factor is removed. It is labelled VERIFIED and must not be written as PROVEN.

Open.

(1) r_∞ itself has no closed form. K isolates the single transcendental input into r_∞; it does not evaluate it.

(2) Whether the exponent s is already in print. The literature route ends at Wong & Li II, which is NOT OBTAINED (§3). The priority position cannot be settled without it, and this notice does not settle it.

(3) A closed form for S_{ζ}. Excluded from one explicitly printed search space (§6.4); not excluded in general. It is carried here under its own new tag, op:cc-szeta-closed-form, and is not filed under op:cc-stokes-closed-form: the latter, created at v1.5 out of the demoted Theorem 3.7(iii), asks whether the CC-channel connection-coefficient *ratio matches the Riemann–Hilbert datum of P_V/D₅^(1) at the V_quad τ-parameter, whereas the former asks whether one number admits a multiplicative closed form in a stated basis. Both mention Stokes data; they are different questions, and one name for two objects is the trap §6.0 forbids. The relation between them is stated at §6.4 and is not a merger.

(4) The V_quad normalisation map, which every comparison of Borel-plane constants across the two normalisations still waits on (§6.5). The target is the Painlevé V transcendent on the Sakai surface D₅^(1), and that identification is itself conjectural — the P-III(D₆) naming was corrected at v1.4 and the identification marked conjectural at v1.5. Working material in this repository still says P-III(D₆); it is stale and must not be copied forward.

(5) The singularity type at ξ₀. op:xi0-d3-direct was withdrawn as vacuous at v1.6 — not closed, not answered — and replaced by op:xi0-singularity-type, which is the live problem: the radius is now proved at every d (§2), and the type is untouched by that proof (§5, §8).

(6) Whether the generating-function operator and the V_quad Borel-plane datum determine one another. New at v1.7, and untagged. The operator L_d annihilating Σ_n Q_n z^n has, at d = 2, Katz invariant 1/2 at z = 0 for every admissible coefficient vector, so its multiset always contains 1/2; van der Put–Saito's D̃₅/P_V row prints no 1/2, and the row is therefore excluded outright, together with six others (§7.2, Tier 1, confirmed by two readings of the printed page). The three surviving rows are PIII(D₈), PIII(D₇), PIII(D₆), selected by deg a = 0, 1, 2 (§7.3, Tier 2, self-derived only), with Channel Theory's own a ≡ 1 falling in the first. A matching multiset is necessary, not sufficient: §7 excludes rows and assigns none, so this neither supports nor disputes item 4, and the two have not been shown to be the same object (§7.0, §7.5, §7.6).

Not formalised. The Lean development carries seven sorrys and zero discharged obligations. lake build succeeding shows the statements typecheck; it shows nothing about provability. No result in Channel Theory is machine-checked, and this notice does not claim formal verification.

1. Erratum and version stack

Read downward for history only. Entries for v1.4, v1.5 and v1.6 are quoted from the deposited descriptions of records 20585624, 22717792 and 22782807, fetched on 2026-09-19 — those versions are not in this repository (see the box below).

Version — Version DOI — Published — Disposition

v1.1 — 10.5281/zenodo.19941679 — — — superseded

v1.2 — 10.5281/zenodo.19951331 — — — superseded

v1.3 — 10.5281/zenodo.19972394 — 2026-05-02 — superseded

v1.4 — 10.5281/zenodo.20585624 — 2026-06-07 — superseded

v1.5 — 10.5281/zenodo.22717792 — 2026-09-12 — superseded

v1.6 — 10.5281/zenodo.22782807 — 2026-09-16 — the current published version

v1.7 — — — — — this notice

The concept record 10.5281/zenodo.19941678 currently resolves to version 1.6, and DataCite lists exactly the six HasVersion identifiers above, so v1.7 is the correct next version number. (Read 2026-09-19 from the concept record and the v1.6 record, both listed in §10; the concept DOI is taken from the conceptdoi / parent field, never from a record number.)

v1.1 → v1.2. The v1.1 cross-degree candidate c(d) = 2√((d−1)!) — which agrees with d = 2 by coincidence — was empirically falsified at d = 4: it predicts ≈ 4.899 against a measured 4, ≈ 22 % disagreement (Remark 3.3.E).

v1.3 (2026-05-02). Purely additive framing revision; nothing rewritten or retracted. Added §3.5 (rem:h4-median), §3.6, and op:cc-median-resurgence-execute. Promoted the cross-degree formula to Conjecture 3.3.A★, ξ₀(b) = d/β_d^{1/d}, proven at d = 2, verified at d = 4, d = 3 deferred to op:xi0-d3-direct.

v1.4 (2026-06-07) — two corrections. (1) The EBR ξ₀ upgrade. For positivity families b(n) > 0 (n ≥ 1), the identity ξ₀ = d/β_d^{1/d} was proved for the physical generating-function object by the holonomic/positivity argument of the companion EBR preprint 10.5281/zenodo.20564079 §3 (D-finite G; leading coefficient a_{2d}(s) = d^d s^{2d}(d^d − β_d s), roots {0, R}; Pringsheim), with scope positive-b families, physical object, symbolic + verified-to-d6 + Lean-checked algebraic layer d = 2–5, not a symbolic-degree formal proof. That superseded the Conjecture-3.3.A★ status for the positive-b case only. (2) Surface-type correction. All references — body, keywords and description — were corrected from Painlevé III(D₆) to the Painlevé V transcendent on the Sakai surface D₅^(1) (W(A₃^(1)), δ = −1/2 ≠ 0). Channel Theory was the last deposit carrying the stale P-III(D₆) root claim.

v1.5 (2026-09-12) — a demotion. Clause (iii) of Theorem 3.7, the match between the CC-channel connection-coefficient ratio and the Riemann–Hilbert datum of P_V/D₅^(1) at the V_quad τ-parameter, is not a theorem of this paper and became the open problem op:cc-stokes-closed-form. Two grounds: the imported surface-type premise is itself conjectural (companion paper Conjecture 4.1, 10.5281/zenodo.20455089, read at v1.2), and the cited run stores a comparison its own verdict did not incorporate — a factor of about two accounted for by an explicit halving in the source, with ~1.7 % unexplained. v1.5 also withdrew as non-evidential a Domb–Sykes sentence that rounded two endpoints agreeing to two digits into a three-digit "range", and corrected five citations that pinned a version in which the cited object was not yet a conjecture. The v1.4 sentence "both corrections are additive/clarifying; no … claim is retracted" does not describe v1.5.

v1.6 (2026-09-16) — five defects repaired; a build, labelling and open-problem erratum. (1) The v1.5 PDF was the draft build, watermarked "DRAFT — NOT DEPOSITED", its date line stalled at "2026-06-07 (v1.4, draft)" and its changelog ending at v1.3 — front matter, not text. (2) op:xi0-d3-direct withdrawn as vacuous, replaced by op:xi0-singularity-type, with rem:d3-vacuous recording the withdrawal (see §5). (3) A citation gap: 10.5281/zenodo.20542162 (deposited 2026-06-04) derives the slope-1/d edge polynomial χ_d(c) = 1 + (−1)^{d+1}(β_d/d^d) c^d symbolically and d-free for all d ≥ 2, with only β_d appearing on the edge; it is now cited at Conjecture 3.3.A★ and op:xi0-degree-d, and that problem is restated — no per-degree computation remains, and the residual is analytic rather than algebraic. (4) Every cross-reference to a proposition, conjecture, remark, definition, example or open problem rendered as "Theorem N" in v1.0–v1.5 (110 sites), because the environments share one counter; the numbered blocks themselves were always correct. Readers of v1.0–v1.5 must treat "Theorem N.N" in running text as naming whatever class the numbered block declares. (5) Falsifiers added to op:cc-median-resurgence-execute and op:cc-formal-borel, the former also gaining a vacuity pre-check — hold β₂ fixed, vary the lower-order coefficients, and confirm that S_{ζ*} actually moves — and all surviving §9 cost estimates marked unverified.

v1.7 (this notice) changes five things.

(1) §2 Attribution. Conjecture 3.3.A★ is retired and attributed. This replaces the v1.4 EBR grounding, which held only for positive b and only for the physical object; the classical route needs no positivity hypothesis at all.

(2) §3 The exponent. s = β_{d−1}/β_d + (d−1)/2 is stated with its derivation and its priority position, including that Wong & Li II is NOT OBTAINED.

(3) §4 K and r_∞. The closed form, and r_∞ identified as exactly the constant the classical turning-point method normalises out of view.

(4) §5 The vacuity explanation. A one-line structural reason generalising and de-empiricising rem:d3-vacuous: v1.6 established the phenomenon for ξ₀ by a coefficient sweep; §5 derives it for ξ₀ and ρ from two proved statements, with no sweep.

(5) §6 The Borel material. ζ* = 2ξ₀ is an action difference, not a change of variable; op:cc-median-resurgence-execute is restated to name the series it concerns; and a pre-registered negative result is recorded against a search space printed in full, filed under a new tag op:cc-szeta-closed-form kept deliberately separate from op:cc-stokes-closed-form (§0, §6.4).

### What was fetched, and what still was not Channel Theory v1.4, v1.5 and v1.6 are not in this repository — the newest in-repo source is v1.3.1, and the v1.3.1 claims record points at pcf-research/channel/…, which does not exist on this machine. The deposited descriptions were therefore fetched from the records themselves on 2026-09-19 with their bytes and hashes recorded in §10: v1.5 and v1.6 from the Zenodo API, v1.3 and v1.4 from DataCite after zenodo.org began returning HTTP 504 on every further request. Everything in the stack above is quoted from that deposited text. Still not obtained, and therefore not quoted: * The v1.5 and v1.6 PDFs. Both file endpoints returned HTTP 504 (api/ records/…/files/…/content and the classic records/…/files/…?download=1). So §9's falsifier statements and their numeric thresholds have not been read — v1.6's description says both open problems now carry one, and §6.3 below says only that, not what the threshold is. * The v1.4 description may be partial. DataCite returned a single 5808-byte description for it; the Zenodo record carries the full HTML, which could not be fetched. The v1.4 text quoted above is also retained verbatim inside the v1.6 description, which is the copy actually used. A correction to this session's own earlier finding. Before the records were fetched, op:xi0-singularity-type was reported as having zero occurrences and was not cited. That was true of the repository and false of the corpus: the tag was created at v1.6 and is real. A repo-wide search establishes absence from the repo, not absence from the published record.

2. Attribution: Conjecture 3.3.A★ is not a conjecture

The statement. With b(n) = β_d n^d + …, β_d ≠ 0, b(k) ≠ 0 for k ≥ 1:

Displayed: lim_{n→∞} | Q_n / (dn)! |^{1/n} = |β_d| / d^d,

so B(w) = Σ_{n≥0} Q_n w^n / Γ(dn+1) has radius of convergence d^d/|β_d| in w, and in the uniformiser ζ = w^{1/d}

Displayed: ξ₀ = d / |β_d|^{1/d}, and at d = 2, ξ₀ = 2/√β₂.

This is prior art. Write the recurrence in the classical form Q_{n+1} + a_n Q_n + b_n Q_{n−1} = 0 with a_n = −b(n+1) ∼ −β_d n^d and b_n = −1, so that in Gautschi's notation α = d and β = 0. Hypotheses (2.2) and (2.8) hold, and the Newton–Puiseux vertex P₁ = (1, d) lies above the segment P₀ = (0,0) — P₂ = (2,0) for every d ≥ 1, so case (a) applies and the ratio asymptotics follow.

Cited to: W. Gautschi, Computational aspects of three-term recurrence relations, SIAM Review 9 (1967), Theorem 2.3(a), p. 35 (Perron–Kreuser) and Theorem 1.1, p. 31 (Pincherle); DLMF §3.6(ii) for the same dichotomy. Both were read from the sources themselves, including a page image of p. 35; see the bibliography in §10.

Gautschi's condition (2.8) constrains the exponents α, β to be real. It does not constrain the coefficients, so complex β_d is inside the classical statement.

Retire the conjecture label. Conjecture 3.3.A★ asserted ξ₀(b) = d/β_d^{1/d} for every degree-d PCF in scope, with the status proven at d = 2, verified at d = 4, d = 3 deferred. That tiered status is withdrawn. The identity holds at every d ≥ 1, classically by Perron–Kreuser plus Pincherle, and independently by an elementary proof carried in the AEAL record — thm:radius, proved without Gamma asymptotics, its Step 3 using a combinatorial multinomial sandwich rather than Stirling (PROVEN). Both routes need only (H): r_∞ ≠ 0.

This supersedes, for this purpose, the EBR positivity upgrade as the grounding. The v1.4 grounding (10.5281/zenodo.20564079 §3) proves the identity only for positivity families b(n) > 0 (n ≥ 1), only for the physical generating-function object, and with a Lean-checked algebraic layer covering d = 2–5 — by its own §8 scope statement, not a symbolic-degree formal proof. The route stated here needs no positivity hypothesis, is not restricted to the physical object, and carries no degree ceiling; the EBR argument remains a valid independent proof on its own narrower scope and is not withdrawn. What (H) asserts is exactly that Q_n is not the minimal solution of the recurrence; the minimal subspace has codimension one, so (H) is generic. That Pincherle reading is interpretive and load-bearing on nothing (STRUCTURAL). Positivity of b re-enters only as the cheapest sufficient condition for (H): if b(n) > 0 for all n ≥ 1 then r_n is strictly increasing with r_n ≥ 1 (PROVEN), and it is then also bounded above by exp Σ_{k≥1} 1/(b(k)b(k+1)) (PROVEN), the positivity being load-bearing in that bound — three of six sign-changing b violate it outright.

Do not let this paragraph migrate into a method statement. Perron–Kreuser-plus-Pincherle is the classical route and is cited here as prior art. Channel Theory's own (H) comes from the positivity proposition, not from Pincherle, and the upper bound uses no minimal-solution, Pincherle or Perron–Kreuser input at any step. A method paragraph led by Pincherle would also invite the Birkhoff–Trjitzinsky rigour question that §3 exists to close.

What §2 does not close. §2 closes the algebraic part of op:xi0-degree-d and nothing more. v1.6 had already restated that problem as having no per-degree computation remaining and an analytic residual; that analytic residual is open, and its name is op:xi0-singularity-type — the type of the singularity at ξ₀, and indeed whether ξ₀ is a singularity of the Borel transform at all rather than only the radius the recurrence fixes. A proof of where the radius sits is not a proof of what sits there. Nothing in §2 touches it, and op:xi0-degree-d must not be reported as closed on the strength of §2 (§8).

3. The exponent, and the priority position

The statement.

Displayed: Q_n / Γ(dn+1) = K · (β_d/d^d)^n · n^s · (1 + O(1/n)), s = β_{d−1}/β_d + (d−1)/2,

equivalently, as an indicial exponent in the Borel plane, ρ_d = −s − 1 = −(d+1)/2 − β_{d−1}/β_d, which at d = 2 is the ρ = −3/2 − β₁/β₂ carried since v1.0 (for V_quad, β₂ = 3, β₁ = 1, giving ρ = −11/6).

Derivation, in outline. Q_n = r_n B_n exactly, with B_n = ∏_{k≤n} b(k) = β_d^n (n!)^d ∏_i Γ(n+1−r_i)/Γ(1−r_i) after factoring b(n) = β_d ∏_i (n − r_i); Gauss multiplication converts (n!)^d against Γ(dn+1), and the d Gamma ratios contribute n^{−Σ r_i} = n^{β_{d−1}/β_d} through Σ_i r_i = −β_{d−1}/β_d, while multiplication supplies the (d−1)/2. The one classical ingredient quoted rather than proved is Γ(z+a)/Γ(z+b) ∼ z^{a−b}, DLMF (5.11.12); with that quoted, the growth law is PROVEN (thm:growth).

Numerically confirmed independently at d = 4 over eight quartic representatives, at dps ≥ 60 and n to 20000, with Richardson extrapolation, and with both pre-registered vacuity arms: varying β_0 … β_{d−2} leaves s unmoved beyond fit error, varying β_{d−1} moves it as predicted (VERIFIED).

3.1 Priority position — stated plainly

DLMF §2.9(ii) gives the exponent explicitly only for bounded coefficients, and routes this degree away. Equation (2.9.6) gives α_j = (f₁ρ_j + g₁)/(f₀ρ_j + 2g₀) with ρ_j the roots of (2.9.5) — but only under f(n) ∼ Σ_s f_s n^{−s}, g(n) ∼ Σ_s g_s n^{−s}, g₀ ≠ 0. Here f(n) = −b(n+2) grows like n^d, so for every d ≥ 1 that expansion, and with it f₀, does not exist, and those clauses do not apply. DLMF then routes exactly this class elsewhere, at (2.9.14): "in which P and Q are any integers see Wong and Li (1992a)." Both equation numbers and the (2.9.14) deferral are present in the hashed capture of DLMF §2.9 listed in §10.

Wong & Li II: NOT OBTAINED. R. Wong and H. Li, Asymptotic Expansions for Second-Order Linear Difference Equations, II, Studies in Applied Mathematics 87 (1992) 289–324, DOI 10.1002/sapm1992874289. Paywalled; the publisher returned HTTP 403; it was not purchased and no mirror was used. Whether s is already in print there, and whether a connection constant is given there in closed form, are NOT ESTABLISHED (INSPECTED).

The asymmetry must be stated with it, as a line and not as a footnote: the unread article cannot reach s, which is derived and independently verified here, and cannot reach the Borel framing; it could bear only on a closed form for the amplitude.

This notice is not gated on obtaining it. The exponent is derived here and verified independently of the literature, and the r_∞ framing rests on Wong & Zhao §3, which is held and hashed (§10). Only a closed form for K could be affected. The article is therefore left NOT OBTAINED, recorded as such, and a future version may settle priority if a copy is ever obtained through non-purchase channels; the priority position stated here must not be softened in the meantime.

The suffix and the numeral are load-bearing. DLMF's "Wong and Li (1992a)" is the paper titled II, in Studies in Applied Mathematics. DLMF's "1992b" is a different paper, J. Comput. Appl. Math. 41 (1992) 65–94, which covers the bounded case and is therefore not ours. Quote the full citation including the word linear and the numeral II; a compressed citation here selects the wrong paper.

3.2 Nothing here rests on Birkhoff–Trjitzinsky

The shape ρ^n n^s (1 + O(1/n)) is Birkhoff–Trjitzinsky's normal-solution shape (Acta Math. 60 (1933), Fundamental Theorem §9, p. 69), which gives existence and shape but no formula for s in the β_k. B–T is cited for that provenance and for nothing else. This must be said in the same breath as the citation, because the standard survey objects to B–T on rigour grounds:

"The major objection to the use of the Birkhoff–Trjitzinsky results is that they may not be rigorous, since gaps are alleged to exist in the complicated proofs." — A. M. Odlyzko, Asymptotic Enumeration Methods, p. 77.

A referee who checks that page reads this. The growth rate here is Perron–Kreuser via Gautschi, the exponent s is derived directly, and the upper bound on r_∞ is elementary. Nothing rests on B–T.

4. K and r_∞

The closed form. With b(n) = β_d ∏_{i=1}^{d} (n − r_i),

Displayed: K = r_∞ · (2π)^{(d−1)/2} / ( √d · ∏_{i=1}^{d} Γ(1 − r_i)).

Label: VERIFIED, never PROVEN. The derivation is complete except for the quoted classical Gamma ratio and is recorded as STRUCTURAL; the form agrees with the numerically computed limit of Q_n/Γ(dn+1) to between 109.66 and 114.69 decimal digits for all eight test polynomials spanning d = 2, 3, 4, including cases with negative K and with sign-changing b (VERIFIED, pre-registered falsifier at 20 digits did not fire); and the vacuity control — recomputing K with the ∏_i Γ(1 − r_i) factor omitted — collapses the agreement from ~110 digits to at most 0.75 digits in every case. The test is therefore sensitive to the quantity the hypothesis is about.

r_∞ is the constant the classical method normalises away. Classical difference-equation asymptotics fixes solutions only up to a multiplicative connection coefficient; K supplies that coefficient, with the single transcendental input isolated into r_∞.

That this is a structural feature of the classical route, and not an oversight in one survey, is recorded twice:

— Absence, with positive controls fired first. The growth law, the exponent s, and any explicit leading constant are NOT FOUND anywhere in Wong & Zhao §3 (PDF pp. 12–20) on a full-text read. Six positive controls were fired first, so the absence test was not vacuous (INSPECTED).

— The structural reason. At (3.23) that section defines K_n by K_{n+1}/K_{n−1} = c_n and sets x_n = y_n/K_n; K_n therefore absorbs exactly the product growth, and Theorems 3.1–3.3 then describe x_n by uniform Airy/Bessel expansions near transition points. It is turning-point theory in a parameter: the growth constant is normalised out of view in order to reach turning-point behaviour, and K_0, K_1 are left depending on the particular sequence (STRUCTURAL).

Source, held and hashed, version-pinned: R. Wong and Y.-Q. Zhao, Recent Advances in Asymptotic Analysis, Analysis and Applications 20 (2022) 1103–1146, DOI 10.1142/S0219530522400012; preprint arXiv:2204.09305v1, 464879 bytes, CC-BY-4.0; the full sha256 is in §10. The version pin is deliberate: the read was of v1.

The connection-constant statement, cited from the sources actually held, with the attribution split as the page has it. On p. 77 Odlyzko writes:

"Wimp and Zeilberger point out that it is usually easy to show that the largest of the terms of the form (9.35) does show up with a nonzero coefficient, and so determines the asymptotics of a_n up to a multiplicative constant. However, the Birkhoff–Trjitzinsky method does not in general provide any techniques for determining that constant."

The first sentence is Odlyzko reporting Wimp and Zeilberger [384]; only the second is his own. Citing the whole passage to Odlyzko misattributes the first half. Verified from a page image re-obtained from the author's site, not from any intermediate record. The PDF and the page image are listed with their sha256 in §10, and the reading was checked at 5 of 5 controls, three of them negative.

Retained alongside it, not replaced by it: G. Nemes (2026), arXiv:2508.15246v2, abstract and §1 p. 3, on connection coefficients being often treated as unknowns in other methods and at best computed numerically (INSPECTED; see §10). Two independent sources for one statement. Odlyzko is the stronger for this point because it is about Birkhoff–Trjitzinsky specifically; Nemes is the more recent.

A third held source, Ibrahim & Salvy, Positivity certificates for linear recurrences (SODA 2024, arXiv:2306.05930v2, CC-BY-4.0; see §10), must be quoted only in its weaker printed form — that the constant is one they do not know how to compute, not that it is not computable.

5. The vacuity explanation

One line replaces an empirical coefficient sweep:

ξ₀ reads only β_d, and ρ reads only β_d and β_{d−1}. Any two families sharing their top two coefficients therefore share both invariants exactly, and no test built on ξ₀ and ρ alone can separate them.

This is immediate from §2 and §3: ξ₀ = d/|β_d|^{1/d} and ρ = −(d+1)/2 − β_{d−1}/β_d. It is structural, not empirical, and it does not depend on degree, on the discriminant, or on which representatives were sampled.

It explains, without a sweep, the phenomena the earlier versions recorded empirically: the K-SCAN marginal coincidence between V_quad and QL15 — both β₂ = 3, hence both ξ₀ = 2/√3 to 200 digits — where the same β₂ forces the same ξ₀ without forcing the same Painlevé label (Remark 3.3.C); and the non-injectivity recorded as Proposition 3.3.B, where QL01 and QL02 share both ξ₀ = 2 and ρ = −5/2 and split only at a₂. The same structure is what the pre-registered vacuity arms of the d = 4 exponent run measured directly.

The consequence for the bridge tiering is that a B1 witness — a β_d-only witness — is by construction the weakest tier, and cannot be strengthened by more ξ₀ data at any precision. Separation requires a coordinate that reads below β_{d−1}.

This generalises and de-empiricises rem:d3-vacuous. That remark was added at v1.6 to record the withdrawal of op:xi0-d3-direct as vacuous, and its evidence is a coefficient sweep: holding β₃ fixed and varying β₂, β₁, β₀ over −1000…+999 moves ξ₀ by 6.85 × 10⁻¹⁸, while varying β₃ alone moves it by 1.26 × 10⁻¹ (v1.6 description, defect (2)). That measurement is at d = 3 and is about ξ₀ only. The two lines above derive the same phenomenon, for every d, for ξ₀ and ρ, from two proved statements and with no sweep at all. The sweep is retained as independent confirmation; it is no longer the reason. v1.6 already states the transferable form — "an observable that depends on less data than the hypothesis it is posed to test cannot test it … it applies to open problems in this corpus that have not yet been examined for it" — and v1.6's own vacuity pre-check for op:cc-median-resurgence-execute (hold β₂ fixed, vary the lower-order coefficients, confirm S_{ζ} moves) is an instance of it. Whether S_{ζ} passes that pre-check is not settled here. ξ₀ and ρ provably do not move; S_{ζ*} is a different object and nothing above decides it either way. The v1.6 citation repair is the algebraic half of the same fact: 10.5281/zenodo.20542162 derives χ_d(c) = 1 + (−1)^{d+1}(β_d/d^d) c^d symbolically and d-free, with only β_d on the edge.

6. The Borel material

6.0 Naming prohibition — binding on this notice and everything downstream

K is the amplitude at ξ₀ = 2/√3. S_{ζ} is the Stokes constant at ζ = 2ξ₀ = 4/√3. They sit at points a factor of two apart in the action. Neither name may ever be used for the other — not in prose, not in code, not in output filenames. Any text that migrates out of this section carries this prohibition with it.

6.1 ζ* = 2ξ₀ is an action difference, not a change of variable

ξ₀ = |c| = 2/√β₂ is the action of a single formal solution: the slope-1/2 characteristic root in exp(c/u), with c² = 4/β₂. The quantity ζ* = |c₊ − c₋| = 2|c| = 2ξ₀ = 4/√3 is the action difference between the two conjugate formal solutions. The two numbers are different objects, at different points of the Borel plane, and no change of variable relates them.

This is not an inference from the numbers. The Borel conventions were extracted verbatim from the pipeline sources and are identical across them — Borel variable ζ ≡ w, the series being transformed the coefficients a_k of S(u), normalisation k! = Γ(k+1), uniformiser u = √z — which is exactly what excludes the "same singularity in different variables" reading. The decisive statement is in the CC-channel pipeline's Padé–Borel source, which gives zeta* = 2·c0 = 4/sqrt(3) and justifies it as the action of the partner formal solution. Classification: a different singularity (STRUCTURAL).

6.2 The halving, and the ~1.7 % residual

The explicit halving is in the earlier recovery source; its own comment deliberates and contradicts itself, and the G2 pipeline resolves it against the halving. The previously unexplained ~1.7 % residual is fully accounted for by two effects together: comparison against the halved target, plus root-test truncation bias at k ≈ 196 (K_FORMAL = 200, samples k = 193 … 200, with convergence only O(ln k / k)). G2 at K = 5000 with conformal Padé reduces the disagreement to about seven digits: 2.309400429346603600679460442221… against 4/√3 = 2.309401076758503058….

No numerical re-derivation of the residual was performed in the session that established this; the account is STRUCTURAL.

6.3 op:cc-median-resurgence-execute, restated

The v1.3 statement of this open problem did not name the series it acts on, and named a Painlevé target that has since moved. Restated:

6.4 A negative result for S_{ζ*}, against a search space printed in full

The space is printed in full below, with no ellipsis, because a printed basis is what lets a reader check it for internal degeneracy and an elided one is what hides it. That is not rhetoric: the first version of this search was run in a space containing Γ(1/6) alongside Γ(1/3), π, 2 and 3, and that space is degenerate. Legendre duplication at z = 1/6 together with reflection at 1/3 gives

Displayed: Γ(1/6) = 2^(2/3) · √3 · Γ(1/3)² / (2√π)

(proved symbolically; |difference| = 0.0 at dps 80, PROVEN), so PSLQ returned that identity — with coefficient exactly zero on log C — for the target and for all three decoys alike. The search never tested the target. Its vacuity pre-check nevertheless reported the required three decoys rejected, one control accepted and so passed for the wrong reason. That first stage is VOID, not negative, and its result is withdrawn rather than edited.

The corrected space, complete:

Displayed: v = [ log C, log 2, log 3, log π, log Γ(1/3), 1 ] seeking integers (m, a, b, c, d, f) with m ≠ 0 such that m·log C + a·log 2 + b·log 3 + c·log π + d·log Γ(1/3) + f = 0 bounds: |coefficient| ≤ 10^6 1 ≤ |m| ≤ 12 dps 120, D_trust = 100 cost = n_nonzero · log10(max|coeff|) ≤ 0.40 · D_trust = 40

Γ(1/6) was removed as redundant, so the corrected space is strictly smaller than the degenerate one and no closed form representable in the original space is lost. The bounds are unchanged from the withdrawn stage, deliberately. Acceptance required all four of: a relation within bounds; cost ≤ 40; stability at 90 and at 80 digits; and reconstruction of the target to ≥ 95 digits at dps 150.

The pre-registered result — a statement about a search, not about the constant:

No multiplicative relation C = ± 2^a 3^b π^c Γ(1/3)^d e^f exists with all coefficients bounded by 10^6, 1 ≤ |m| ≤ 12 and digit cost ≤ 40, against C = 8.1273367954950723671… known to 100 decimal digits. No candidate was returned at any bound, so no rejected candidate has a digit cost to report. The constants were first shown mutually independent by a degeneracy pre-check that returned no relation at any bound; all three decoys were rejected on their own merits; and the positive control 4π²/(3Γ(1/3)) was recognised at cost 1.5051, at every bound. Label: VERIFIED. This excludes that space. It is not evidence that C has no closed form, and it says nothing about spaces containing other Gamma values, other algebraic irrationalities, polylogarithms, or ζ(3). (dps 120.)

This negative is filed under a new tag, op:cc-szeta-closed-form, and not under op:cc-stokes-closed-form. The two are kept apart deliberately:

— op:cc-szeta-closed-form — does C (equivalently S_{ζ*} = 2πi·C, the amplitude at 2ξ₀) admit a multiplicative closed form? The §6.4 result is a negative against the one space printed above and is recorded as the first entry under this tag, together with its stated space, so that any later search is read as widening a printed space rather than as a fresh question.

— op:cc-stokes-closed-form — does the CC-channel connection-coefficient ratio match the Riemann–Hilbert datum of P_V/D₅^(1) at the V_quad τ-parameter? This is an identification question inherited from the demoted Theorem 3.7(iii) at v1.5.

How they relate, without merging. A closed form for C would be evidence bearing on op:cc-stokes-closed-form, because the Riemann–Hilbert datum is expected to be expressible in Gamma values; and the identification, if ever established, would supply a candidate for C. But neither implies the other: C could have a closed form with the identification false, and the identification could hold with C outside every Gamma basis. The §6.4 negative therefore says nothing about op:cc-stokes-closed-form, and must not be cited as though it did. They both mention Stokes data; that is a shared subject, not a shared question — precisely the one-name-two-objects failure §6.0 forbids for K and S_{ζ*}, applied here at the level of problems rather than constants.

6.5 The normalisation caveat that travels with C

C is read in V_quad native normalisation, with S_{ζ} = 2πi·C and the convention *leading B[Φ] = 1. The V_quad → Painlevé normalisation map remains OPEN. Anything found for C is therefore a closed form of that number in that normalisation, and may not be compared with quantities computed in a sectorial basis under a different convention without the map. This caveat is not optional and is not separable from the negative result above.

7. The formal type of the generating-function operator

7.0 The object, and what it is not

Summing the recurrence against z^n gives, for the generating function f(z) = Σ_n Q_n z^n of the denominators,

[ 1 − z·b(θ+1) − z²·a(θ+2) ] f = 1, θ = z d/dz,

with a ≡ 1 in Channel Theory's own recurrence and general deg a = e allowed below. Write L_d := z·b(θ+1) + z²·a(θ+2) − 1. The question asked here is the formal type of L_d at d = deg b = 2: its singular points, their Newton polygons, and the resulting Katz invariants, compared against the ten-row classification of van der Put–Saito, Table 2.1. At d = 2 the operator has rank 2, which is the setting that table classifies; the comparison is made at d = 2 for that reason and is not extended to other degrees.

This is not the object of §0 item 4. That item concerns whether the CC-channel connection-coefficient ratio matches the Riemann–Hilbert datum of P_V/D₅^(1) at the V_quad τ-parameter — a statement about monodromy data of a different object, carried under op:cc-stokes-closed-form and conjectural since v1.5. L_d is the operator annihilating a generating function of denominators. Both are labelled by Painlevé equations; that is a shared vocabulary, not a shared object, and §6.0's prohibition applies here as it does to K and S_{ζ*}. Whether the two determine one another is open and untagged; none may be invented for it.

7.1 What the printed page says

Every quotation below was verified against a page image identified by the folio printed on the page, not by index arithmetic.

Folio 2634, §2.2: the objects classified are local families M(u) of differential modules represented by d/dz + A(z,u) with A a 2 × 2 matrix of trace 0 on P¹; "A singular point p with Katz invariant r(p)…"; and "We will not number these ten families, but indicate them by their Katz invariants, e.g., (0,0,0,0), (0,0,1), …, (0,−,3/2), (−,−,3), (−,−,5/2)." The identification of the table's r(·) columns with Katz invariants is therefore the source's own, not an assumption imported here.

7.2 Tier 1 — independently confirmed

This paragraph is Tier 1: independently confirmed, VERIFIED.

At z = 0 the Newton polygon of L_d at d = 2 gives Katz invariant 1/2 for every admissible coefficient vector — the value does not depend on the coefficients, only on the degrees and the non-vanishing of the leading ones. The multiset of Katz invariants of L_d therefore always contains 1/2.

The D̃₅ / P_V row of Table 2.1 prints r(0) = 0, r(1) = 0, r(∞) = 1, r(t) = −. No entry in that row is 1/2. Hence the multiset of L_d is never that row's multiset, and

D̃₅ / P_V is not compatible with L_d for any admissible coefficient vector at d = 2 — not for a sampled family, for all of them.

The same one-line test disposes of six further rows, being exactly those whose printed entries contain no 1/2: D̃₄/PVI (0,0,0,0), D̃₆/PIII(D6) (1,−,1,−), Ẽ₆/PIV (0,−,2,−), Ẽ₇/PII (0,−,3/2,−), Ẽ₇/PII (−,−,3,−) and Ẽ₈/PI (−,−,5/2,−). Seven of the ten rows go at once, and the three that survive are precisely the three containing 1/2.

Confirmation. This exclusion has been reached by two readings of the printed table: one in this corpus, and one by an isolated reader given only the operator, its conventions, and page images of folios 2634–2637, with no access to this work, its conclusions or its vocabulary, which reached the exclusion without being told it. A third, independent transcription of the ten rows was made during preparation; all three agree in every row and column, including which entries carry the printed dash.

7.3 Tier 2 — self-derived, not independently confirmed

This paragraph is Tier 2: self-derived, and NOT independently confirmed. STRUCTURAL.

The three surviving rows are reached, and are selected by deg a:

e = deg a — Katz multiset — surviving row

0 — {1/2, 1/2} — D̃₈ / PIII(D₈)

1 — {1/2, 1} — D̃₇ / PIII(D₇)

2 — {0, 0, 1/2} — D̃₆ / PV_deg = PIII(D₆)

Channel Theory's own recurrence is a ≡ 1, i.e. e = 0, and so falls in the PIII(D₈) line of this table. The isolated reading covered deg a = 2 only, so it confirms the Tier 1 exclusion but not this set; the single multiset it reported, {0,0,1/2}, is the third line above and neither confirms nor contradicts the other two. This tier rests on one derivation.

7.4 Tier 3 — self-derived by a contaminated re-derivation

This paragraph is Tier 3: self-derived by a re-derivation that was contaminated. It is the weakest statement in §7 and is NOT independently confirmed. STRUCTURAL.

Generically the surviving row depends only on (α₂, α₁). On the codimension-3 locus a(1) = a(2) = 0 and b(1) = 0 the point at infinity becomes ordinary, and the resulting multiset matches no row of Table 2.1 at all. The derivation that produced this ran in a workspace another process was writing into, and it corrected an earlier error of its own before arriving here; neither isolated reading reaches this tier, and both state explicitly that they did not classify the coefficient subloci on which an apparent singularity may be removed by a common factor. A reader should not assume the exceptional locus has been characterised.

7.5 A matching multiset is a necessary condition only

Equality of Katz multisets is necessary, not sufficient, for L_d to sit in a given row's family. The procedure of §7 therefore excludes rows and assigns none. A mismatch settles the question and is VERIFIED, being an equality check against a printed table; a match does not, because it leaves open whether L_d actually lies in the corresponding moduli family, which would need the classification's sufficiency and not merely its invariants. That is why every exclusion above is VERIFIED and every surviving row is STRUCTURAL. Nothing in §7 places L_d in any family, and no sentence of it may be restated as though it did.

7.6 The record's own Painlevé history, stated and not adjudicated

This record has carried two different Painlevé labels, and §7's surviving set falls on both sides of the change. Both facts are stated here; neither is adjudicated.

— v1.0–v1.3 carried P-III(D₆). That label lies inside the surviving set of §7.3.

— v1.4 replaced it with the Painlevé V transcendent on the Sakai surface D₅^(1), and v1.5 marked that identification conjectural. That label lies outside the surviving set, in the row §7.2 excludes.

It does not follow that the v1.4 correction was wrong, for two independent reasons, either of which alone is sufficient:

(1) A row exclusion is not a row assignment (§7.5). §7 removes D̃₅/P_V from the rows L_d can meet; it does not place L_d in PIII(D₆) or anywhere else, and a label that survives §7 is not thereby supported.

(2) The two labels are about a different object (§7.0). They name the V_quad Borel-plane datum, not L_d, and the two have not been shown to determine one another.

This notice asserts no Painlevé label for V_quad. It repeats the record's history, records where §7's surviving set falls relative to it, and stops there. The stale P-III(D₆) wording still present in working material remains stale and must not be copied forward on the strength of §7.

7.7 What §7 does not settle

— It does not establish sufficiency (§7.5), so it assigns no row.

— It does not dispute, or support, the V_quad Painlevé-V identification (§7.0, §7.6), and is not evidence about it in either direction.

— It does not extend beyond d = deg b = 2, where the rank-2 setting of the table applies (§7.0).

— It rests on one published table, read three times, not on an independent derivation of the classification.

— Tiers 2 and 3 rest on one derivation each (§7.3, §7.4); only Tier 1 has been reached twice. ---
